questions: Q1: What CLI interface should hlx inspect netsuite expose?
Q2: What CLI interface should hlx run expose?
Q3: Should the CLI expose an --env flag for either command?
Q4: What basePath should hlx run use -- the default /api/inspect or an override?
Q5: Does either command need NetSuite-specific error handling or a custom timeout?

answers.answer: hlx inspect netsuite supports two modes via body type discriminator: (a) SuiteQL queries matching the db subcommand interface: --repo <name> --query '<SuiteQL>' (recommended), --query-file <path> (complex queries), and positional query argument (convenience); (b) Script log retrieval with --logs flag: --repo <name> --logs --script-id <id> [--date-from <date>] [--date-to <date>] [--log-type <type>]. Default mode (no --logs) is SuiteQL query. New handler file src/inspect/netsuite.ts follows db.ts pattern (~20 lines for both modes).
evidence: src/inspect/db.ts:5-12 -- cmdDb(config, repo, query) pattern with resolveRepo + hxFetch POST
product/product.md SCN-01: 'hlx inspect netsuite --repo <name> "SELECT id, companyname FROM customer"'
helix-global-server AD-5: single endpoint with { type: 'query' | 'logs' } discriminator

answers.answer: hlx run is a new top-level command (not under inspect) following the configOrHelp pattern from src/index.ts:26-35. Interface: hlx run --repo <name> '<code>' (inline), hlx run --repo <name> --script-file <path> (from file), optional --modules <comma-separated>. Handler follows resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST -> console.log pattern. New module at src/run/index.ts with new case in src/index.ts switch. Both hlx run and hlx inspect netsuite use the default basePath '/api/inspect' since the server routes both under the inspect prefix (helix-global-server AD-1).
evidence: src/index.ts:81-156 -- no 'run' case exists; configOrHelp pattern established at L26-35
helix-global-server AD-1: both surfaces under /api/inspect/ prefix

answers.answer: No. The environment (PRODUCTION vs SANDBOX) is determined server-side from the inspection token's nsEnv claim (set by configureInspectionForStep in the orchestrator). Exposing an --env flag would be misleading and insecure -- the server ignores client-specified environments. The agent doesn't need to know which environment it's querying. A human-facing --env flag is a future consideration.
evidence: helix-global-server AD-3: environment embedded in signed JWT, not request body
session.ts: JWT signed with authJwtSecret -- cannot be forged by agent
product/product.md: '--env flag' listed under 'Features Explicitly Out of Scope'

answers.answer: hlx run uses the default basePath '/api/inspect' because the server endpoint is POST /api/inspect/:repositoryId/run (under the inspect prefix, per helix-global-server AD-1). No basePath override needed. The hxFetch call is: hxFetch(config, '/${repoId}/run', { method: 'POST', body: { code, modules? } }).
evidence: helix-global-server AD-1: both surfaces under /api/inspect/ prefix
src/inspect/db.ts: existing pattern uses '/${repoId}/database' relative to default basePath

answers.answer: No NetSuite-specific error handling needed. The existing hxFetch() covers 429 (rate limit with Retry-After), 401 (unauthorized), and 5xx (server errors) with 3-attempt retry and exponential backoff (http.ts:71-130). The server translates NetSuite errors into standard HTTP errors with descriptive messages. For timeout, the existing 30s REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (http.ts:5) is adequate for MVP -- the server-side RESTlet timeout is 25s (helix-global-server TD-6), leaving headroom. A custom --timeout flag is deferred to Round 2 for long-running SuiteScript.
evidence: src/lib/http.ts:71-130 -- retry logic handles 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff, Retry-After support
helix-global-server TD-6 -- 25s RESTlet timeout; 15s OAuth2 timeout
Existing subcommands (db, logs, api) have no type-specific error handling in the CLI

statement: helix-cli needs two additions: (1) hlx inspect netsuite -- new case in inspect router (src/inspect/index.ts) + new handler file (src/inspect/netsuite.ts) following the db.ts 12-line template for SuiteQL queries and a --logs mode for script log retrieval, and (2) hlx run -- new top-level case in main dispatcher (src/index.ts) + new module (src/run/index.ts) for arbitrary SuiteScript execution with --repo, --script-file, and --modules flags. Both use the default basePath '/api/inspect' because the server routes both surfaces under the inspect prefix. Both use existing hxFetch with dual-mode auth, 3-attempt retry, and 30s timeout. No --env flag (token-bounded). No NetSuite-specific error handling. Zero new dependencies. All line references verified against current source.
